title: 6.3.10 Car on a Ramp
description: Build a two-wheeled car using HingeJoints and drive it up a ramp with WASD. The harder of the two A14 options.

steps.title: Ground + ramp
steps.instructions: Two static sprites: a flat ground and a tilted ramp. Set the ramp's .rotation in degrees to tilt it (moSHion rotation is in degrees, not radians).
hints: The Sprite docs chapter (right drawer → Docs tab) covers static colliders.
ramp.rotation = -20 tilts up to the right; positive values tilt the other way.

steps.title: Chassis + wheels
steps.instructions: Chassis: one dynamic rectangle. Two wheels: dynamic sprites with a `diameter` so they're circular. Then give both wheels, the ground and the ramp a `.friction` of 1. Every sprite starts at friction 0, which is ice, and two touching sprites grip with a mix of both values (5.2.11), so a grippy wheel on icy ground still slides.
hints: Place the wheels slightly below the chassis corners so the joints have room.
The Physics docs chapter explains dynamic vs static bodies.
Four lines: leftWheel.friction = 1; rightWheel.friction = 1; ground.friction = 1; ramp.friction = 1;

steps.title: Join the wheels with HingeJoint
steps.instructions: new HingeJoint(leftWheel, chassis) and again for the right wheel. A HingeJoint pins two sprites at one point and lets them turn around it, like 6.3.8's pendulum. The pin goes where the FIRST sprite is, so name the wheel first: the pin lands at the wheel's centre, and the wheel can turn on it like an axle while staying fixed to the chassis.
hints: 6.3.8 (Worked Example: Swinging Pendulum) uses new HingeJoint(anchor, rod): the rod turns around the anchor, the first sprite.
Wheel first, chassis second. With the chassis first, the pin sits in the middle of the chassis and the wheel swings around it like the pendulum's rod instead of turning in place.

steps.title: Drive with WASD
steps.instructions: In draw(), use kb.pressing('a') / kb.pressing('d') to set chassis.vel.x (positive = right, negative = left, 0 = stop). The grader looks for an assignment to .vel.x (or an applyForce call).
hints: Open the Input docs chapter for kb.pressing. Don't use arrow keys: they scroll the editor.

vel.x sets horizontal velocity directly each frame; with the friction from step 2 the wheels roll as the chassis moves (at friction 0 they slide along without turning). Spinning the wheels alone does not move the car.

requirements.title: Uses HingeJoint
requirements.description: Join a wheel to the chassis with at least one new HingeJoint(...). A WheelJoint, from the Joints chapter of the docs drawer, also counts. Help: 6.3.8 (Worked Example: Swinging Pendulum)

requirements.title: Static geometry exists
requirements.description: Create at least one 'static' sprite (ground or ramp). Help: 5.2.11 (Bounciness and Friction)

requirements.title: Tilted ramp via rotation
requirements.description: Assign to .rotation: tilting the ramp. Help: 5.1.10 (Sprite property tour: pos, rotation, scale)

requirements.title: Gravity enabled
requirements.description: Assign a positive value to world.gravity.y. Help: 5.2.6 (Gravity)

requirements.title: WASD drives the car
requirements.description: Use kb.pressing with 'a' or 'd' inside draw(). Help: 5.1.15 (Keyboard Movement)

requirements.title: Drives the car
requirements.description: Assign to the chassis's .vel.x (or call applyForce on it) to move the car. Help: 5.1.16 (Velocity: vel.x and vel.y)
